mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 4.5% for four consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and corporate margin potential, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in periods where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both fall >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of months where both INDPRO and HOUST decline by over 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in the effective federal funds rate below 2% during a recession (UNRATE > 6%) signals an aggressive easing cycle, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: aggressive monetary easing in deep recession
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline during episodes where FEDFUNDS falls below 2% and UNRATE exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% signals heightened precautionary behavior, which reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods where RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for two months in a row.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% signals labor market tightening, which boosts wage pressure and inflation expectations, ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate higher earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not deliver positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of months where PAYEMS grows by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly rise of at least 2% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based expansion in economic activity, which lifts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both rise >2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of months where both INDPRO and HOUST increase by over 2%.
